evals.name: agent-readable-readme
evals.prompt: Write a README section explaining how to run our CLI tool 'deploykit' which has commands: init, plan, apply, rollback. It will be read primarily by AI coding agents working in the repo.
evals.expected_output: Unambiguous, agent-oriented writing: explicit command sequences with expected outcomes, states preconditions, avoids prose ambiguity, defines error handling expectations, structured for machine parsing (consistent formatting).
assertions: Commands are documented with explicit invocation syntax and expected outcome per command
Preconditions or ordering constraints are stated explicitly (e.g. must run init before apply)
Writing avoids ambiguous pronouns/vague references that would confuse an automated reader

evals.name: vague-to-spec
evals.prompt: Rewrite this vague requirement into something an AI coding agent could implement without asking questions: 'make the dashboard load faster and look nicer'.
evals.expected_output: Converts vague goals into measurable, testable spec items: concrete performance metric with target (e.g. LCP < 2s), specific UI changes enumerated, scope boundaries stated, verification method included.
assertions: Performance goal is made measurable with a specific metric and numeric target
'Look nicer' is replaced with concrete, enumerable UI changes
Includes how completion would be verified or tested

evals.name: ops-runbook
evals.prompt: Write runbook steps for: when the nightly data import fails, an operator should be able to fix it. The importer pulls from an SFTP server, transforms CSVs, and loads into Postgres.
evals.expected_output: Agent/operator-executable steps: explicit diagnostic checks in order (check logs location, verify SFTP connectivity, check file format, check DB constraints), each step with pass/fail signal and next action, no unstated assumptions.
assertions: Diagnostic steps appear in a logical ordered sequence covering the three failure domains (network/SFTP, file format/transformation, database)
Each step indicates how to determine success or failure
No critical steps left implicit (e.g. does not assume the reader knows where logs live)
